slides.0.title: 🌊 Calabria
slides.0.subtitle: A Treasury of Ancient Grapes at the Toe of Italy
slides.1.title: 🌊 Calabria at a Glance
slides.1.content:
The “toe” at the southern tip of the Italian boot, surrounded by water on three sides: the Ionian Sea to the east, the Tyrrhenian Sea to the west, and the Strait of Messina separating it from Sicily to the south. Ancient Greek settlers called it “Oenotria” (Enotria) — the land of the vines.

🗺️
Topography
Hills and mountains make up over 90%, with the Southern Apennines (Pollino, Sila, Aspromonte, Catena Costiera) running through the region
🌡️
Climate
Mediterranean on the coast, with continental influence inland
🏅
Appellations
9 DOCs and no DOCG; most production is wine without origin
🍇
Grapes
Nearly 90% red; Gaglioppo covers more than half the vineyards
slides.2.title: 🗺️ Calabria Key DOC Interactive Map
slides.3.title: 🏆 Cirò DOC — the Legendary Wine of Olympians
slides.3.content:
Calabria’s oldest (1969) and most productive DOC, on the central Ionian coast. Krimisa, one of the most famous wines of the Greek period, was reportedly given as a prize to winners of the ancient Olympic Games; its name is believed to derive from the Greek colony of Cremissa, in today’s Cirò area.

🔴 Cirò Rosso

Min. 80% Gaglioppo, Calabria’s benchmark red. Red cherry, strawberry and earthy minerality, with high acidity and tannin. May be labelled Classico, Superiore (min. 13.5% ABV), Riserva (min. 2 years’ ageing) and their combinations.

🌸 Cirò Rosato

Min. 80% Gaglioppo, a fresh rosé with strawberry, redcurrant and watermelon — great with seafood and summer dishes, the taste of the Calabrian coast.

🤍 Cirò Bianco

Min. 80% Greco Bianco, a light, easy-drinking white with citrus, almond blossom and salty minerality — perfect with Calabrian swordfish and seafood.
slides.4.title: 🍇 Gaglioppo — Calabria’s Signature Red
slides.4.content:
Gaglioppo is one of Italy’s most ancient grapes, considered native to Calabria; it is Calabria’s signature and principal red grape, planted on more than half the vineyards. Its name is often explained as “beautiful foot”. It is high in acidity and tannin.

Standard style

🍷 Cirò Rosso style

🎨 Colour: medium garnet, paler than many southern Italian reds

🌹 Aromas: red cherry, strawberry, rose petal, a touch of earthy minerality

👅 Palate: high acidity, high tannin

🏷️ Producers: Librandi, A Vita, Ippolito 1845

Riserva

🏆 Aged Riserva style

⏱️ Ageing: Cirò Rosso Riserva min. 2 years

🌹 Aromas: dried herbs, leather, cedar, roast meat

👅 Palate: tannins round out with age, with layered complexity

🏷️ Producers: Ippolito 1845, Ceraudo
slides.5.title: 🏺 Calabria’s Other Important Grapes
slides.5.content:
🍇 Magliocco

Status: the other important traditional red grape

Note: Magliocco Canino and Magliocco Dolce have similar names and are often confused locally

Style: deep colour, full body

Appellations: Terre di Cosenza, Lamezia, Savuto and other DOCs

🍯 Greco Bianco

Status: Calabria’s main white grape

The truth: genetically identical to Malvasia di Lipari, also known as Greco Bianco di Gerace; a different variety from Campania’s Greco

Use: ideal for appassimento; the star of Greco di Bianco DOC and the base of Cirò Bianco

Note: the name “Greco Bianco” is often used for other grapes too

🌸 Nerello Cappuccio and others

Nerello Cappuccio: a red grape with a significant presence in Calabria

Others: Greco Nero, Nerello Mascalese, Mantonico Bianco, Pecorello, Guarnaccia Bianca

Naming chaos: Calabrians use the same name for different grapes and different names for the same grape around the region, making it one of Italy’s most confusing regions for grape names
slides.6.title: 🍯 Greco di Bianco DOC — Sweet Passito White
slides.6.content:
A small, prestigious appellation for sweet passito wine, made around the village of Bianco on the southern Ionian coast. Min. 95% Greco Bianco; golden-amber, with complex aromas and flavours, min. 14% ABV, sweetness balanced by fresh acidity.

🍇 Get the names right

Greco Bianco is the grape; Greco di Bianco is the DOC; Bianco is the town. Greco Bianco is genetically identical to Malvasia di Lipari and ideal for appassimento.

🍯 Tasting and pairing

Semi-sweet to sweet, not dry. Serve at 12-14°C in small glasses and sip slowly. Pair with amaretti, Gorgonzola, fruit tarts and dried figs.
slides.7.title: 🏷️ Other Important DOCs
slides.7.content:
🍷 Lamezia DOC

Main grapes: Gaglioppo, Magliocco, Greco Nero, Nerello Cappuccio

Style: rich, deep-coloured, powerful reds, suited to hearty beef and lamb stews

Location: the central Tyrrhenian coast, on the Sant'Eufemia plain near Lamezia Terme

🌿 Bivongi DOC

Main grapes: Gaglioppo, Greco Nero (red); Greco Bianco, Mantonico Bianco (white)

Key fact: a small appellation on the southern Ionian coast

Location: the southern Ionian coast, near the ancient Greek city of Locri

🏔️ Savuto DOC

Main grapes: blends of Gaglioppo, Greco Nero and Magliocco

Key fact: a hill area in the Savuto valley

Location: Cosenza and Catanzaro provinces, on the Tyrrhenian side
slides.8.title: 🌶️ Calabria Food Pairing Guide
slides.8.content:
Calabria is Italy’s “kingdom of chilli”, and its fiery spreadable 'nduja is famous worldwide. Seafood from the Ionian coast and swordfish from the Tyrrhenian combine two maritime food cultures into a unique pairing map.

🌶️ 'Nduja pasta

Spaghetti con 'Nduja — Calabria’s fiery soul food
🍷 With: Cirò Rosso Classico Superiore
Lively acidity balances the heat, red fruit cuts the fat

🐟 Grilled swordfish (Pesce Spada)

The Tyrrhenian coast’s most iconic seafood dish
🍷 With: Cirò Bianco or Greco Bianco
Fresh minerality lifts the fish

🧀 Fileja con 'Nduja e Caciocavallo

Local twisted pasta + 'nduja + Calabrian smoked cheese
🍷 With: Magliocco, Lamezia DOC
A deep, full body matches the power of the spicy cheese

🍯 Pairing Greco di Bianco

Traditional amaretti, Gorgonzola
🍷 With: Greco di Bianco DOC
A golden-amber passito whose sweetness is balanced by fresh acidity
slides.9.title: 🏺 The History of Calabrian Wine
slides.9.content:
From the Greek “Oenotria” to today — an ancient land of wine

Ancient Greece
Oenotria (Enotria): ancient Greek settlers called Calabria “the land of the vines”. The famous wine Krimisa was reportedly given as a prize to winners of the ancient Olympic Games; its name is believed to derive from the Greek colony of Cremissa, in today’s Cirò area
16th century
Renaissance records: Sante Lancerio, cellar master of Pope Paul III, and the wine scholar Andrea Bacci both wrote about Calabrian wines
19th-20th c.
The bulk-wine era: for much of the 19th and 20th centuries Calabria was mainly known for vini da taglio (bulk blending wine); in 1969 Cirò became Calabria’s first DOC
Today
Rising quality: estates such as Librandi have taken Calabrian wine to international markets, and several former DOCs have merged into Terre di Cosenza DOC. Most production is still wine without origin

slides.10.title: 🍇 Gaglioppo in Depth
slides.10.content:
🧬 Origin

One of Italy’s most ancient grapes, considered native to Calabria

The name is often explained as “beautiful foot” (Gaglioppo = beautiful foot)

Calabria’s signature and principal red grape, on more than half the vineyards

📊 Characteristics

Acidity: high

Tannin: high

Main appellation: Cirò DOC (Rosso and Rosato min. 80%)

Training: alberello is Calabria’s dominant training system

How Gaglioppo ages: from fresh fruit to complex leather

🌸 Youth (1-3 years)

Red cherry, fresh strawberry, rose petal, lively acidity

Best with: seafood, salads, light dishes

🍷 Maturity (4-8 years)

Dried herbs, leather, cedar, salty minerality

Best with: Classico Superiore and roast chicken

🏆 Old age (9+ years)

Leather, tobacco, earth, complex minerality

Best with: Riserva and grilled lamb chops
slides.11.title: 🏖️ Topography, Climate, Soils and the Cirò Categories
slides.11.content:
Hills and mountains make up over 90% of Calabria, with the Southern Apennines running through it and water on three sides. Cirò lies on the central Ionian coast, and its Classico subzone covers only the municipalities of Cirò and Cirò Marina.

🪨

Extremely diverse soils

Sandy gravels

Clays of marine origin

Alluvial soils

Limestone and sandstone

Coast: Mediterranean

Inland: continental influence

slides.12.content:

Cirò (oldest and most productive), Greco di Bianco (sweet passito white), Bivongi, Lamezia, Melissa, Sant'Anna di Isola Capo Rizzuto, Savuto, Scavigna, Terre di Cosenza

IGTs: Calabria, Val di Neto

🗺️ Terre di Cosenza DOC

Merges several former DOCs: Colline del Crati, Condoleo, Donnici, Esaro, Pollino, San Vito di Luzzi, Verbicaro

slides.14.title: 🌶️ 'Nduja Culture + Pairing Guide + Two-Sea Tour
slides.14.content:
'Nduja is Calabria’s fiery spreadable pork sausage, seasoned with Calabrian chilli; the town of Spilinga is its home. Four pairing scenarios:

🍝 'Nduja pasta

Spaghetti con 'Nduja (creamy spicy sauce)
🍷 With: Cirò Rosso Classico Superiore
High acidity balances the creaminess, red fruit tames the heat

🥖 Spread on toast

Bruschetta con 'Nduja (starter)
🍷 With: Cirò Rosato (chilled)
Fresh acidity and strawberry refresh, and the chill softens the chilli’s bite

🍕 'Nduja pizza

Pizza con 'Nduja e Burrata
🍷 With: Magliocco, Lamezia DOC
Rich fruit and full body match the heat

🥩 BBQ

Grilled pork ribs with 'nduja sauce
🍷 With: Cirò Rosso Riserva
Firm tannins meet the char of the grill in perfect balance
